messages.content:
The sky appears blue due to a phenomenon called **Rayleigh scattering**.

When sunlight reaches Earth's atmosphere, it collides with gas molecules (mostly nitrogen and oxygen). Sunlight contains all colors of the visible spectrum, but shorter wavelengths (blue and violet) scatter much more strongly than longer wavelengths (red and yellow). This scattered blue light is dispersed in all directions, reaching our eyes from every part of the sky.

While violet light actually scatters even more than blue, we see the sky as blue because the Sun emits more blue light than violet, and human eyes are much more sensitive to blue.
